# Fixtures

Documents the erase and redaction suites run against. Everything here is either
generated by this repository or taken from a public, synthetic test corpus —
nothing is a real person's or a real company's document.

## `letter.pdf` — generated

Built by [`make-fixtures.mjs`](./make-fixtures.mjs); re-run it any time:

```bash
node tests/fixtures/make-fixtures.mjs
```

It is an ordinary-looking A4 letter chosen for the four shapes that have each
broken the eraser at some point, plus one that cannot be solved at all:

| what is on the page | why it is there |
|---|---|
| a bold coloured run with `!` hard against it | an over-wide erase eats the punctuation |
| a short bold heading | a small target must not be over-erased |
| a coloured run with a rule beneath it | the rule is not text and has to survive |
| a run inside a filled colour band | the patch must take the band's colour, not the paper's |
| white lettering baked into a speckled raster strip | tier 2 — no background exists to recover |

Because the page is generated, `cases.json` carries the exact box each run was
drawn at rather than a coordinate measured off a render. A failing case
therefore means the eraser missed, never that a rect was a pixel out.

## `hard/` — from the pdf.js corpus

Three small PDFs covering shapes the letter does not: a rotated page, a
non-origin crop box, and text inside a form XObject. Provenance, hashes and the
upstream URLs are in [`hard/PROVENANCE.md`](./hard/PROVENANCE.md). They are
synthetic constructions from Mozilla's renderer tests (Apache-2.0) and never
enter the shipped bundle.

## Why there are no "real" documents here

There were two: a private individual's CV and a company's internal event email.
Real type and real artefacts make for a better test than anything synthetic, and
while this repository was private that was a reasonable trade.

It stops being reasonable the moment the repository is public. Publishing is
worldwide and permanent — a clone cannot be recalled — and neither the person
whose CV it was nor the company ever agreed to that. So the corpus is generated
now, and the loss of a little realism is the correct price.

If you are adding a fixture: it must be something this project owns, something
generated, or something from a public corpus with its provenance recorded. Never
a document that came from someone's life.
